bull.b: Advancement of a registrational PCNSL program creates a potentially important value inflection beyond early discovery work. Continued enrollment and future combination data could support regulatory submissions if efficacy and safety remain adequate.

Specific dosing and data milestones improve visibility into the development path for emavusertib. The CLL study also evaluates two doses under Project Optimus, helping generate structured evidence for future clinical decisions.

Partner and regulatory relationships can extend Curis’s scientific and development capabilities beyond its small internal workforce. External expertise and agency engagement may improve trial design and support more efficient advancement of oncology candidates.

bear.b: Sustained negative operating and free cash flow means Curis is not self-funding its development programs. Continued dependence on external capital can constrain strategic flexibility and increase the risk of dilution or funding interruptions.

Curis lacks a stable commercial revenue base to offset research costs, and partnered receipts can be uneven. Persistent operating losses and declining or choppy revenue reduce visibility to break-even while clinical investment continues.

Repeated equity financing creates dilution risk and may not fully resolve the funding gap. Dependence on a patient-dosing milestone for additional proceeds also links liquidity to enrollment execution in small, difficult-to-recruit indications.
